title: Statecharts: A Visual Formalism for Complex Systems
evidence: Fetched live: Weizmann Institute research-portal record (weizmann.elsevierpure.com) confirms author David Harel, journal Science of Computer Programming, volume 8, issue 3, pages 231-274, June 1987, DOI 10.1016/0167-6423(87)90035-9; cross-checked against the ScienceDirect landing page and Crossref bibliographic record returning identical metadata.
note: The formalism Stateflow implements: hierarchy, concurrency and broadcast communication added to state-transition diagrams. Named zero-hit anchor for model-c x design; without it the pass's Stateflow citations rest on an uncited ancestor.

title: STATEMATE: A Working Environment for the Development of Complex Reactive Systems
authors: David Harel, Hagi Lachover, Amnon Naamad, Amir Pnueli, Michal Politi, Rivi Sherman, Aharon Shtull-Trauring, Mark Trakhtenbrot
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref bibliographic API (api.crossref.org/works, queried on title+author): container-title 'IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering', volume 16, issue 4, pages 403-414, year 1990, DOI 10.1109/32.54292 — matched against the earlier ICSE-1988 conference version (DOI 10.1109/icse.1988.93720) which Crossref returns as a distinct, earlier record, confirming the journal version is the correct full account.
note: The first shipped tool environment executing statecharts, i-Logix's STATEMATE — direct commercial and technical ancestor of MathWorks Stateflow. Grounds the 'Statemate account' the mission names as required reading alongside the 1987 formalism paper.

title: The STATEMATE Semantics of Statecharts
venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology, 5(4), 293-333
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/235321.235322): title 'The STATEMATE semantics of statecharts', ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology, volume 5, issue 4, pages 293-333, year 1996; ACM DL landing page (dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/235321.235322) returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch but the same DOI/title/venue triple was independently corroborated by the web search result set.
note: The formal, executable semantics that closed the ambiguities left informal in the 1987 paper — the paper a rigorous account of 'what a Stateflow chart IS' actually needs, one level below the visual formalism itself.

title: LUSTRE: A Declarative Language for Real-Time Programming
authors: Paul Caspi, Daniel Pilaud, Nicolas Halbwachs, John A. Plaice
venue: Proceedings of the 14th ACM SIGACT-SIGPLAN Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages (POPL '87), 178-188
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/41625.41641): title 'LUSTRE: a declarative language for real-time programming', authors Caspi/Pilaud/Halbwachs/Plaice, venue POPL '87 proceedings, pages 178-188, year 1987 — matches the ACM DL record dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/41625.41641 named in search results.
note: The founding LUSTRE paper: the synchronous data-flow language SCADE *is*, per the critic panel's own framing. This is the origin the SCADE Suite tool-doc membership (already in the harvest) has no citable ancestor for.

title: The Synchronous Data Flow Programming Language LUSTRE
authors: Nicolas Halbwachs, Paul Caspi, Pascal Raymond, Daniel Pilaud
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=...): title, authors, container-title 'Proceedings of the IEEE', volume 79, issue 9, pages 1305-1320, year 1991, DOI 10.1109/5.97300; IEEE Xplore document page (ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/97300) returned blank on direct fetch (JS-rendered) but its document id (97300) matches the Crossref-resolved DOI suffix, and the same triple was independently returned by two search queries.
note: The comprehensive tutorial/retrospective account of LUSTRE (special issue on synchronous programming) — the paper that explains the compilation-to-automaton pipeline SCADE's qualified code generator descends from.

title: SIGNAL: A Data Flow-Oriented Language for Signal Processing
authors: Paul Le Guernic, Albert Benveniste, Paul Bournai, Thierry Gautier
venue: IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing, 34(2), 362-374
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/tassp.1986.1164809): title 'Signal--A data flow-oriented language for signal processing', authors Le Guernic/Benveniste/Bournai/Gautier, IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing, volume 34, issue 2, pages 362-374, year 1986.
note: The founding SIGNAL paper — the third leg of the synchronous-language triad (LUSTRE/Esterel/SIGNAL) named in the mission and previously entirely absent.

title: Programming Real-Time Applications with SIGNAL
authors: Paul Le Guernic, Thierry Gautier, Michel Le Borgne, Claude Le Maire
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=...): title, all four authors, container-title 'Proceedings of the IEEE', volume 79, issue 9, pages 1321-1336, year 1991, DOI 10.1109/5.97301 — the companion paper to the LUSTRE retrospective in the same special issue, confirmed in the same query pass.
note: SIGNAL's mature-language account, published back-to-back with the LUSTRE retrospective in the 1991 Proceedings of the IEEE synchronous-programming special issue this pass otherwise harvests only via SCADE.

title: The ESTEREL Synchronous Programming Language and its Mathematical Semantics
venue: Seminar on Concurrency (Carnegie-Mellon University, 1984), Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 197, Springer, 389-448
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/3-540-15670-4_19): title, authors Berry/Cosserat, container Lecture Notes in Computer Science / Seminar on Concurrency, pages 389-448, year 1985; corroborated by the Springer chapter landing page URL (link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-15670-4_19) and ACM DL cross-reference (dl.acm.org/doi/10.5555/646723.702721) returned in search results.
note: Esterel's founding paper — the imperative-style third synchronous language, sibling to LUSTRE and SIGNAL, contributed by Gérard Berry who later co-designed SCADE 6 with Colaço and Pagano.

title: The ESTEREL Synchronous Programming Language: Design, Semantics, Implementation
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/0167-6423(92)90005-V): title, authors Berry/Gonthier, journal Science of Computer Programming, volume 19, issue 2, pages 87-152, year 1992 — the same DOI is listed on the ACM DL cross-reference and ScienceDirect page URLs returned by search.
note: The mature, most-cited (1900+ citations) account of Esterel covering compiled-automaton implementation as well as design and semantics — the implementation-lineage counterpart to the 1985 founding paper.

title: The Synchronous Languages 12 Years Later
authors: Albert Benveniste, Paul Caspi, Stephen A. Edwards, Nicolas Halbwachs, Paul Le Guernic, Robert de Simone
evidence: Fetched live via Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/JPROC.2002.805826): title, all six authors, container-title 'Proceedings of the IEEE', volume 91, issue 1, pages 64-83, year 2003; corroborated by a Verimag-hosted author copy URL and the IEEE DOI prefix matching JPROC (IEEE Proceedings) convention.
note: The named 'synchronous-language survey literature' the mission asks for: retrospective on LUSTRE/Esterel/SIGNAL a decade after the 1991 special issue, tracing the path from academic language to certified industrial tools (SCADE among them).

title: Synchronous Programming of Reactive Systems

evidence: Fetched live: Internet Archive catalog record (archive.org/details/synchronousprogr0000halb) confirms title 'Synchronous programming of reactive systems', author Nicolas Halbwachs, publisher Kluwer Academic Publishers (Dordrecht; Boston), year 1993, ISBN 0792393112, xiii+174pp — cross-checked against the Springer catalog redirect (link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4757-2231-4, the book's current Springer-imprint DOI record) and independent Semantic Scholar / OpenLibrary listings, all agreeing on title/author/publisher/year/ISBN.

title: SCADE 6: A Formal Language for Embedded Critical Software Development (invited paper)
authors: Jean-Louis Colaço, Bruno Pagano, Marc Pouzet
venue: 2017 International Symposium on Theoretical Aspects of Software Engineering (TASE)
evidence: Fetched live: TASE 2017 conference's own invited-speakers page (tase2017.i3s.unice.fr/node/7.html) confirms Jean-Louis Colaço's invited talk on SCADE, describing SCADE as 'a development environment for safety critical embedded software used for more than twenty years in various application domains like avionics, nuclear plants, transportation, automotive', and confirms the venue as the 11th (2017) International Symposium on Theoretical Aspects of Software Engineering, Sophia Antipolis; DOI 10.1109/TASE.2017.8285623 confirmed via Crossref bibliographic API.
note: The published account of how LUSTRE's synchronous semantics became the qualified commercial SCADE 6 generator — the exact bridge the critic panel named between the LUSTRE paper and the already-harvested Ansys/Synopsys SCADE Suite tool-doc.

title: Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI), Version 3.0
evidence: Fetched live from fmi-standard.org/news/2022-05-10-fmi-3.0-release/: 'FMI version 3.0, now released by the Modelica Association, is a major milestone for the standard' enabling 'advanced co-simulation, virtual Electronic Control Units (vECUs), the next generation of Digital Twins'; and fmi-standard.org/about/: FMI is maintained by 'the Modelica Association Project (MAP) FMI', operating 'under the roof of the Modelica Association', current project leader Christian Bertsch (Bosch).
note: The vendor-neutral model-exchange/co-simulation standard supported by Simulink, Dymola, SimulationX, AMESim and 170+ tools. D7 previously had zero FMI hits despite 116 tools-process taggings — the critic panel's single most damaging D7 finding.

title: System Structure and Parameterization (SSP), Version 2.0
evidence: Fetched live from ssp-standard.org/docs/2.0/: confirms 'release 2.0 of the System Structure and Parameterization Standard (SSP)', maintained by 'Modelica Association Project "SSP"', described as 'a tool-independent format for the description, packaging and exchange of system structures and their parameterization' with explicit FMI 3.0 support, released 2024-12-20.
note: FMI's sibling co-simulation standard: where FMI packages one model/FMU, SSP describes and parameterizes the composed system of FMUs. Directly answers the mission territory's 'co-simulation standards' line, one level up from FMI itself.
